title: Fall of France 1940 (Fall Gelb / Fall Rot)

briefing.historical: On 10 May 1940 Germany attacked in the West (Fall Gelb). Army Group B invaded the Netherlands and Belgium while Army Group A, with seven panzer divisions, advanced through the Ardennes toward the Meuse (S06, S07). The Allied 1st Army Group, including the French First, Seventh and Ninth Armies and the BEF, advanced into Belgium under Plan D (S13). Sedan was crossed on 13 May (S08), the Channel reached about 20 May, the BEF evacuated from Dunkirk 26 May - 4 June (S11), and Fall Rot opened on 5 June. France signed the armistice on 22 June (S06).
briefing.situation: Play the German offensive, the French defence or the BEF. The Germans must break the Meuse and reach the Channel before the Allies can consolidate; the Allies must hold the Meuse and Paris and preserve their forces. Positions at the start are approximate assembly areas, not surveyed historical deployments. The scenario runs to the armistice, 25 June 1940.

playableNations.summary: Execute Fall Gelb and Fall Rot against numerically comparable Allies with the initiative.
Defend France with a large but poorly coordinated army and a fixed strategic plan.
Command the BEF: a small force far from home with a coast at its back.

sources.citation: thesecondworldwar.org, "Axis order of battle - Army Group A" (Battle of France 1940). Compiled OOB incl. army/corps/division commanders. Internally inconsistent in places (see uncertain list).

thesecondworldwar.org, "Fall Gelb - Axis order of battle" overview page (used for Army Group C: First and Seventh Armies; single-source, lower confidence).

thesecondworldwar.org, "Fall Gelb - Allied order of battle" (French army groups/armies/corps/divisions, BEF, Belgian and Dutch armies). Page structure is partly garbled; only unambiguous assignments used.

Wikipedia, "Order of battle for the Battle of France" (army-group level summary; Belgium ~600,000 / 22 divisions; Netherlands ~240,000 / four corps; Army of the Alps ~35,000). Article flagged by Wikipedia as needing citations.

Wikipedia, "Battle of France" (timeline: 10 May start; Dutch surrender 15 May; Sedan 13 May; Channel ~20 May; Fall Rot 5 Jun; Italy 10 Jun; Paris open city 10 Jun, occupied 14 Jun; St-Valery-en-Caux 12 Jun; Operation Tiger 15 Jun; Reynaud resigns 16 Jun; Cherbourg 18 Jun; armistice 22 Jun, effective 25 Jun 00:35; strength totals).
Wikipedia, "Fall Gelb" (Manstein Plan; Panzergruppe Kleist: XIX Corps 3 Pz, XLI Corps 2 Pz, XV Corps 2 Pz; halt orders 17/22/24 May).
Wikipedia, "Battle of Sedan (1940)" (12 May Sedan reached; 13 May 1st, 2nd, 10th Pz cross Meuse at Gaulier, Donchery, Wadelincourt; 14 May bridge, failed Allied air attacks).

Wikipedia, "Battle of the Netherlands" (10-17 May 1940; main Dutch forces surrender after Rotterdam bombing; Zeeland until 17 May; 9th Panzer, airborne forces). Note: article summary gives 14 May for main surrender; S06 gives 15 May.
Wikipedia, "Battle of Arras (1940)" (21 May; Frankforce: 1st Army Tank Brigade, 5th and 50th Divisions; German 7th Panzer, SS-Totenkopf).
Wikipedia, "Operation Dynamo" (26 May - 4 June 1940; 338,226 evacuated; halt order issued 23 May by Rundstedt, approved by Hitler 24 May, rescinded 26 May; Calais surrendered 26 May).

Wikipedia, "British Expeditionary Force (World War II)" (I Corps 1st/2nd Div; II Corps 3rd/4th Div; 5th Div GHQ; III Corps; Saar Force 51st Highland; 12th/23rd/46th labour divisions; Second BEF June; Operation Cycle 10-13 Jun Le Havre; Operation Aerial 15-25 Jun).
Wikipedia, "Dyle Plan" / French war planning 1920-1940 (Plan D: 1st Army Group = 7th Army, BEF, 1st Army, 9th Army; Dyle line; 7th Army to Breda; 9th Army on the Meuse; 2nd Army Sedan to Maginot).
DHM LeMO, "Besetzung von Belgien 1940" and Wikipedia "Belgium in World War II": Belgian capitulation 28 May 1940 (Leopold III).

Weather Works Inc., "Weather in History: The Evacuation of Dunkirk" (calm seas / low cloud late May - early June 1940; Halder diary 30 May on grounded Luftwaffe). Only qualitative support for weather profile.

Wikipedia, "Beauman Division" (BEF base ports Cherbourg, Brest, Nantes, St Nazaire; Le Havre principal supply/ordnance depot; Rouen sub-area/base depots) and the Despatch of Lord Gort (London Gazette supplement 35305) on BEF lines of communication. Sources differ on whether Brest or Le Havre was the main supply port.

Wikipedia, "Fall Rot" (Weygand Line ~965 km from Sedan to Abbeville with 64 divisions and few reserves; Tenth Army (R. Altmayer); Seventh and Tenth Armies reconstituted 23-28 May; 1st/2nd DCR raised; Second Army Group moved from Alsace-Lorraine to the Somme; small towns fortified as "hedgehogs"). Britannica "Weygand Line" gives about 49 divisions instead of 64 (discrepancy).

Wikipedia, "Henri Dentz" (General Officer Commanding Paris Military Region, 1940) and press/secondary accounts that Gen. Hering, military commander of the Paris District, announced a defence of Paris on 10 June and handed command to Dentz on 13 June before it was left undefended as an open city. The strength of any Paris garrison is NOT sourced.

Wikipedia unit articles "Sturzkampfgeschwader 2", "Sturzkampfgeschwader 77", "Kampfgeschwader 27" (StG 2/StG 77 under VIII. Fliegerkorps, Luftflotte 2; KG 27 under IV. Fliegerkorps, Luftflotte 2). AIRFIELD POSITION POLICY (internal): airfield coordinates are nearest-village/airfield gazetteer values recalled to 0.01 deg; accuracy +/-0.15 deg. Where a Geschwader Stab base lies outside the map bbox, a Gruppe base inside the map is used (KG 2, KG 4, KG 53); KG 51 and KG 55 (all bases outside the bbox) and Lysander squadrons are omitted.

GAME-SCALE ABSTRACTION (internal, not a historical source): manpower, equipment points, morale/experience/organisation values, nation resources and income are nominal game values chosen for balance by type/nation. They are NOT historical strengths.
Modern gazetteer coordinates (Wikipedia/GeoNames, rounded to 0.01 deg) for towns, cities, ports and fortresses. Maginot fortress coordinates are approximate (+/- 0.05 deg).

POSITION POLICY (internal): no source gives division-level start positions. Unit positions are approximate sector/assembly-area anchors inferred from the operational axes in S06-S08 and S13, with a small deterministic spread inside the sector. Every unit position is APPROXIMATE.

BORDER POLICY (internal): initialControl polygons are coarse hand-drawn approximations of 1939/1940 borders (Alsace-Lorraine French, Saar German, Luxembourg unclaimed) and ignore coastline detail; caveat: not survey-accurate.
